newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada preferred peaceful end to Lima crisis.
newsitem.headline: Canada preferred peaceful end to Lima crisis.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Tuesday Canada would have preferred it if Peru had used peaceful means to end the Lima hostage crisis, but nonetheless supported the result.

"We would have of course preferred to see the resolution take place by more peaceful means, but that was simply a preference," Axworthy told reporters after Peruvian troops stormed the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence.
"A judgment call, as we said right from the start, had to be made by the Peruvian government."
He said Canada regretted the loss of life but added: "The result was one that we can support."
Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent was one of the figures involved in negotiations between the Peruvian government and the leftist hostage takers.
Axworthy said he hoped the summit of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Denver in June would be able to address how to prevent similar hostage crises.
